notes: §1985:VII.2.7.3 SR3: 'Data-name-1 must be defined in the Data Division as a one-character data item of the category alphanumeric and must not be defined in the Communication Section, the File Section, or the Report Section.' CapturePadding takes the operand as data-name-1 (a non-constant word), ResolveFiles resolves it through the clause-operand resolver and ScreenPaddingDataName refuses a non-alphanumeric category, a width other than 1 or an ODO under it, and any section but Working-Storage/Local-Storage/Linkage (COBOL6848, 1985 wording at DialectLevel < 2002). Probes at --std 85 (work-rd-04/c9): refused: PIC A, PIC 9, PIC XB (alphanumeric edited), PIC XX (the witness), a File Section item, an ambiguous unqualified name, a level-88 name; accepted and the file written and read back: PIC X, a one-character group and its PIC X child, JUSTIFIED, a Linkage item, a qualified QP OF WR; literals "*", ALL "*", ZERO, '9' accepted, "**" and numeric 9 refused (SR1). Lead outside this rule: an unsubscripted table element (WTE PIC X OCCURS 2) is accepted as data-name-1, where §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR4 says 'Each table element reference must be subscripted except when such reference appears' in four places this is not.

next.reason: 1985 VII.2.7.3 SR3: PADDING CHARACTER data-name-1 'must be defined ... as a one-character data item of the category alphanumeric' outside the Communication, File and Report Sections. 2023 has no PADDING CHARACTER clause (none among the file control entry clauses of §2023:12.4.5; PADDING is not a 2023 reserved word; deleted in 2014 per docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row 7.20), so no 2023 rule carries this requirement.
